messages:
Eli: ACME follow-up — they must have IPv6 egress from their firewall to our Dedicated endpoint and want cert-based client auth. They said they can't do a VPC peering right now. Any creative POC options?
Priya: Short answer: full mTLS termination on our ingress requires Private (VPC) or on-prem today. But we have a couple of hacks for POC: NAT64/DNS64 gateway, or customer-side TLS-terminating proxy that forwards with a signed header.
Ben: NAT64 could let IPv6-only clients reach our IPv4 egress IPs. We run a managed NAT64 in a test region for a few enterprise trials — not production-grade, but OK for a short POC. Requires DNS config on their side.
Nina: If they do a customer proxy that terminates client certs, we need assurance it preserves identity. For security we require either: (a) mutual TLS on their proxy + X-Client-Cert header + HMAC signature of the header, or (b) use our short-lived token exchange where their proxy requests a token from our auth service using mTLS and uses that token to call us.
Eli: Good. They asked about IP rotation — they want a static IPv4 that won't change during the week.
Priya: We can allocate a reserved egress IP for the Dedicated POC (elastic-nat). We'll mark it non-rotating for the POC window. Note: if there's a provider incident we may need to swap with notice.
Ben: For NAT64 option the allowlist they'd add is our NAT64 IPv4 address. We also need to give them DNS instructions (set the A/AAAA mapping to the gateway).
Eli: Can we run NAT64 + a proxy so they get IPv6 to the proxy and mTLS from proxy to us? That's probably the simplest for them.
Nina: Yes — setup: their clients -> IPv6 -> NAT64 gateway -> proxy (terminates mTLS) -> our Dedicated endpoint (IPv4 egress). We'll need network diagram and an ops contact.
Eli: Timeline? ACME wants to test tomorrow morning.
Priya: If we use managed dedicated sandbox + reserved egress IP + quick NAT64 config we can stand up in ~6 hours. If they need Private with native IPv6 and ingress mTLS that'll be ~2-3 days for infra and approvals.
Ben: Pricing: quick NAT64 + reserved IP + 1-week sandbox = typically waived platform fee for strategic deals, ops labor billed if it goes beyond 8 hours of SRE work. I'll flag as "likely no-cost" but put a small ops pass-through if SRE exceeds the window.
Eli: Security questionnaire — what exact docs do we need from them to allow the proxy approach?
Nina: 1) Completed network/security questionnaire (I will send). 2) Proxy cert details and rotation cadence. 3) Expected CIDRs for their internal clients (for audit). 4) Contact for emergency cert revocation.
Eli: Can you draft a one-page checklist I can email?
Nina: On it. Sample checklist snippet for their proxy: ```
- Proxy must validate client certs against customer CA
- Proxy must forward X-Client-Identity header and HMAC(X-Client-Identity + timestamp)
- Proxy must use TLS 1.2+ to our endpoint
- Tokens/certs rotated every 30 days (or provide emergency revoke contact)
```
Eli: They also want a curl example for the token exchange approach.
Priya: Example (proxy side gets token via mTLS, then calls us):
```bash
# fetch token from our auth service (mTLS client cert)
curl --cert /path/proxy.crt --key /path/proxy.key https://auth.redwood.example/v1/token -d 'scope=dedicated.poc'
# use token to call API
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" https://dedi-poc.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Ben: ops-bot will queue the Dedicated sandbox with reserved egress IP if we approve.
ops-bot: dedicated-sandbox:queued id=dp-422 ETA=6h
Eli: Great. I'll propose two parallel tracks to ACME: (1) Fast-track: Dedicated sandbox + reserved IPv4 egress + proxy/NAT64 workaround for IPv6 and token flow. (2) Full-track: Private VPC with native IPv6 + ingress mTLS. We'll offer to start (1) immediately and pivot to (2) if they need true native IPv6.
Eli: Action items: Nina send questionnaire, Ben reserve egress IP and estimate SRE hours, Priya prepare NAT64 DNS instructions and token example. I'll send ACME the proposal and ask which track.
Priya: ack.
Ben: ack.
Nina: ack, sending questionnaire now.
Eli: I'll update here when ACME responds.
